text: Vectera Advisors — House View

slides.title: Key Themes
text: • Core real-estate values are stabilizing after the 2023–2024 repricing; U.S. private funds have turned positive over the past year (see exhibits).
• We favor industrial / logistics and multifamily, remain underweight office, and are selective in retail.
• Leverage discipline and patient deployment into the recovery.

slides.title: Macro & Capital Markets
text: • Global macro is stabilizing; core values are recovering following the significant 2023–2024 repricing.
• U.S. private real estate fund returns have moved back into positive territory over the trailing year (exhibit).
• Cap rates have largely stabilized while the spread over Treasuries has widened, restoring the real-estate risk premium (exhibit).
• Transaction activity is rebounding from cyclical lows as rate volatility eases and bid-ask spreads narrow.
• We maintain leverage discipline and prefer moderate loan-to-value as financing normalizes.

slides.title: Return Backdrop — U.S. Private Real Estate
text: Trailing 3-year returns still carry the drawdown, but the latest quarter and one-year figures have turned positive.

slides.title: Capital Markets — Cap Rates and Rates
text: Cap rates have held broadly stable as Treasury yields settled; the spread has re-widened versus the 2024 trough.

slides.title: Sector Outlook — Forecast NOI Growth
text: Residential and industrial lead forecast income growth; office and retail lag across the horizon.

slides.title: Industrial & Logistics — Overweight
text: • Our top overweight: fundamentals remain tight and rent growth is normalizing from double-digit peaks.
• Vacancy sits well below its long-run average; new supply is moderating after a record delivery wave.
• Focus on infill locations and outdoor / industrial storage.

slides.title: Residential / Multifamily — Favored
text: • A widening own-versus-rent affordability gap supports durable rental demand (exhibit).
• Record new deliveries are peaking and set to taper, easing rent pressure.
• A key area of interest for new capital deployment.

slides.title: Office — Underweight
text: • Transaction cap rates have repriced sharply higher — well above appraisal marks (exhibit).
• A pronounced bifurcation persists; only best-in-class, well-located assets are favored.
• Leasing is improving off a low base, but the recovery is uneven.

slides.title: Retail — Selective
text: • Years of minimal new supply against steady population growth have tightened availability, especially in the Sun Belt (exhibit).
• Grocery-anchored and necessity-based formats are favored for resilient cash flows.
• Discretionary and enclosed-mall formats remain out of favor.

slides.title: Private Real Estate Debt — Opportunistic
text: • Reduced bank lending has widened spreads, creating selective opportunities in senior and mezzanine credit.
• Relevant for dedicated debt mandates; not a focus of core / value-add equity portfolios.

slides.title: Risks We Are Monitoring
text: • A resurgence in rate volatility could re-widen bid-ask spreads and stall the transaction recovery.
• Refinancing of 2020–2021 vintage debt at higher rates remains a sector-wide overhang, most acute in office.
• Slower-than-expected supply absorption in select multifamily submarkets.

slides.title: Positioning Summary
text: • Maintain leverage discipline; prefer moderate loan-to-value.
• Tilt toward industrial / logistics and multifamily; underweight office; be selective in retail.
• Deploy patiently into the recovery as pricing stabilizes.

 not closed by Quarter-end. The funded investments have generated a since-inception net IRR of 9.2% and a 1.44x net

 target real estate allocation. The Portfolio seeks long-term net nominal returns in excess of the CPERS Custom
 Benchmark (NCREIF ODCE, net of fees), and is diversified across property type, geography and strategy.

One Financial Plaza (Chicago office) was written down on lower submarket comparables and a near-term lease expiry, while Bayfront Apartments (San Diego) was held roughly flat as concessions offset rent growth, and Prairie Logistics (Kansas City) contributed positively, partially offsetting the office drag, with leverage remaining conservative at ~28% LTV.
Beacon Diversified Property Trust. The Fund returned 1.12% net, with Quarter-end NAV of $41.9M and 28.0% LTV.

Gateway Logistics Center (Dallas) was marked up following the completion of lease-up to 97% occupancy at rents ahead of underwriting, while Harbor 40 Distribution (Savannah) appreciated modestly on a new 10-year lease to an investment-grade tenant, and Cedar Ridge Infill (Inland Empire) was held flat pending a planned expansion; leverage remained conservative at approximately 31% loan-to-value.
Harborview Industrial Fund. The Fund returned 1.31% net, with Quarter-end NAV of $43.3M and 44.5% LTV.

Eastgate Industrial (Phoenix) reached stabilized occupancy and was marked up materially, while Northline Logistics (Nashville) appreciated on completion of a build-to-suit, and the Fund is unlevered at the fund level.

Meridian Opportunity Fund V was the Portfolio's largest detractor. The Fund returned -1.53% net, with Quarter-end NAV of $30.2M and 42.2% LTV. Income of -$31,854, appreciation of -$468,730 and a fee credit of $31,290 resulted in a -$469,294 dollar contribution.

Northgate Logistics Partners - $40.0M, approved October 2025.
The approval remained open and was not carried as a funded holding at Quarter-end. No performance figures are assigned to this commitment.

Northgate Logistics Partners is a value-add industrial fund targeting the acquisition and repositioning of infill logistics and outdoor-storage assets in high-growth Sun Belt and Mountain-West markets, with a strategy focused on lease-up, mark-to-market of below-market rents, and selective development completion.
Ridgeline Value Fund IV - $25.0M, approved November 2025.
The approval remained open and was not carried as a funded holding at Quarter-end. No performance figures are assigned to this commitment.

Ridgeline Value Fund IV is the fourth vintage in Ridgeline Capital's diversified value-add series, targeting the acquisition and repositioning of multifamily and mixed-use assets in supply-constrained coastal and Mountain-West metros, with a strategy that emphasizes operational improvement, unit renovation, and mark-to-market of below-market rents, as well as selective ground-up completion.
The previously approved $25.0M commitment to Alder Creek Multifamily Fund III was withdrawn during the Quarter. The Fund closed at its hard cap without an allocation to the client.
The previously approved $30.0M commitment to Sentinel Logistics Income Fund lapsed during the Quarter. The approval expired unexercised on 30 November 2025 and is not being renewed.

The market deck notes that core real-estate values are stabilizing after the 2023–2024 repricing, with U.S. private funds turning positive over the past year and a preference for industrial / logistics and multifamily, while remaining underweight office and selective in retail. The market deck highlights that a resurgence in rate volatility could re-widen bid-ask spreads and stall the transaction recovery, while refinancing of 2020–2021 vintage debt at higher rates remains a sector-wide overhang, most acute in office, and slower-than-expected supply absorption is noted in select multifamily submarkets. The market deck's positioning guidance is to maintain leverage discipline, prefer moderate loan-to-value, tilt toward industrial / logistics and multifamily, underweight office, be selective in retail, and deploy capital patiently as pricing stabilizes. Broad private real-estate funds returned 1.0% net in the latest quarter and 3.3% over 1-Yr. At 25Q4, the NPI value-weighted cap rate was ~4.6%, compared to ~4.2% for the 10-year Treasury yield. The Portfolio's largest property exposures are Industrial at 36.2% and Apartment at 23.5%, with the deck forecasting 2026-27 (p.a.) NOI growth of ~1.3% for industrial and ~1.4% for residential, and reiterating a house-view preference for industrial / logistics and multifamily, underweight office, and selectivity in retail. The office exhibit reports, at 25Q4, appraisal cap rate ~5.6% versus transaction cap rate ~7.7%, and the transaction/appraisal gap widened from 0.7 to 2.1 percentage points.

value: Market Outlook — Fourth Quarter 2025
Vectera Advisors — House View
Key Themes
• Core real-estate values are stabilizing after the 2023–2024 repricing; U.S. private funds have turned positive over the past year (see exhibits).
• We favor industrial / logistics and multifamily, remain underweight office, and are selective in retail.
• Leverage discipline and patient deployment into the recovery.
Macro & Capital Markets
• Global macro is stabilizing; core values are recovering following the significant 2023–2024 repricing.
• U.S. private real estate fund returns have moved back into positive territory over the trailing year (exhibit).
• Cap rates have largely stabilized while the spread over Treasuries has widened, restoring the real-estate risk premium (exhibit).
• Transaction activity is rebounding from cyclical lows as rate volatility eases and bid-ask spreads narrow.
• We maintain leverage discipline and prefer moderate loan-to-value as financing normalizes.
Return Backdrop — U.S. Private Real Estate
Trailing 3-year returns still carry the drawdown, but the latest quarter and one-year figures have turned positive.

• Our top overweight: fundamentals remain tight and rent growth is normalizing from double-digit peaks.
• Vacancy sits well below its long-run average; new supply is moderating after a record delivery wave.
• Focus on infill locations and outdoor / industrial storage.
Residential / Multifamily — Favored
• A widening own-versus-rent affordability gap supports durable rental demand (exhibit).
• Record new deliveries are peaking and set to taper, easing rent pressure.
• A key area of interest for new capital deployment.

value: Private Real Estate Debt — Opportunistic
• Reduced bank lending has widened spreads, creating selective opportunities in senior and mezzanine credit.
• Relevant for dedicated debt mandates; not a focus of core / value-add equity portfolios.
Risks We Are Monitoring
• A resurgence in rate volatility could re-widen bid-ask spreads and stall the transaction recovery.
• Refinancing of 2020–2021 vintage debt at higher rates remains a sector-wide overhang, most acute in office.
• Slower-than-expected supply absorption in select multifamily submarkets.
Positioning Summary
• Maintain leverage discipline; prefer moderate loan-to-value.
• Tilt toward industrial / logistics and multifamily; underweight office; be selective in retail.
• Deploy patiently into the recovery as pricing stabilizes.
